name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield back above 5.3% on 13 Nov and 2-year at its highest since October 2023 as BoE rise bets grow
state: The 10-year gilt yield rose above 5.3% on 13 Nov, its highest since late October, but is about 6bp lower than a month earlier, well inside the 40bp monthly move line (Trading Economics). Two-year yields reached 5.005%, the highest since October 2023, after September GDP beat forecasts and markets priced an 82% chance of a December rate rise (MarketScreener, 13 Nov). The 30-year gilt is near 5.8%, close to multi-decade highs, so Watch is kept.
for_you: Higher gilt yields raise government borrowing costs and tend to feed into fixed mortgage and loan pricing within weeks. Pension schemes and funds holding gilts see valuations move with yields.
rubric_hit: Watch: 30-year gilt near multi-decade highs (~5.8%); 10y monthly move about -6bp, under the 40bp line

sources.title: MarketScreener (Dow Jones) — U.K. Gilt Yields Accelerate on Rate-Hike Expectations
Trading Economics — UK 10 Year Bond Yield

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
